answer: Reciprocal latency ledger: each identity must answer randomized peer probes within a median round-trip bound, and its past responses form a trellis of timing signatures others check before transacting. A clone cannot copy timing because it shares one host's queue, so replies drift into a recognizable echo of the original. Sustained probe coverage across a meadow of independent peers is required. Attacker cost: one machine, one timing profile—clones collapse under correlated latency.
